drivers.name: AVer Pro-AV PTZ Camera (PTZ310/330)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: AVer Pro-AV PTZ310 / PTZ330 family. Combines VISCA-over-IP (UDP 52381) for power, PTZ motion, and position inquiries with AVer's HTTP CGI (port 80, /storks) for image quality (shutter, iris, gain, white balance, color temperature, saturation, contrast, sharpness), AI features (SmartShoot, SmartFraming), bulk status query, RTMP streaming, mirror/flip, and reboot. For the TR615 and TR211 / TR315 / TR335 tracking cameras use 'aver_tr'; for other AVer cameras, the generic 'visca_ip' driver.

help.overview: AVer PTZ310 / PTZ330 broadcast PTZ cameras. Common in houses of worship, lecture capture, courtroom recording, and corporate AV. Image quality (gain, iris, shutter, white balance, color temperature, sharpness, mirror/flip) and AVer's SmartShoot / SmartFraming AI features are controlled over HTTP. Power, pan/tilt/zoom motion, and position inquiries use VISCA-over-IP.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and place it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. The driver opens TWO connections: VISCA-over-IP on UDP 52381 and HTTP on TCP 80. Both must be reachable.
3. Most CGI commands require no authentication. The Reboot and Factory Reset commands require Basic auth and only work on the PTZ-S310 / PTZ-S330 SKUs — fill in the username/password fields if you need them.
4. VISCA-over-IP supports multiple controllers per camera, so OpenAVC can co-exist with a hardware joystick or other control surface.

compatible_models.notes: Verified against AVer's VISCA Specification 3.3 (April 2025) and the PTZ310/330 HTTP CGI Commands document (June 2022). Both transports use the same camera IP. Reboot and Factory Reset require Basic auth on PTZ-S310/S330 SKUs; configure a username/password on those models.

drivers.name: AVer TR Auto Tracking Camera (TR615, TR335 / TR315 / TR211)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: AVer TR615 and TR211 / TR315 / TR335 AI auto tracking PTZ cameras. VISCA over IP (UDP 52381) for power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets, exposure, white balance, tally, freeze and auto tracking, with every value the camera reports read back; the HTTP CGI for tracking mode, preset save and recall, saturation, contrast, flip, theme mode and factory reset.

help.overview: AVer TR-series AI auto tracking PTZ cameras for lecture capture and presenter tracking. Power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets, exposure, white balance, tally, freeze and auto tracking use VISCA over IP; tracking mode, preset save and recall, saturation, contrast, flip, theme mode and factory reset use the camera's web interface (HTTP).
help.setup:
1. Give the camera a fixed IP address.
2. The driver uses two connections to the camera: HTTP on TCP 80 and VISCA over IP on UDP 52381. If you changed the VISCA Port Number on the camera, enter the same number here.
3. Enter the camera's web interface username and password. The camera asks for them on tracking mode and factory reset; without them those are unavailable and the device page says so.
4. If HTTPS Only is turned on in the camera, turn on HTTPS here and set the HTTP Port to 443.

compatible_models.notes: Built from the TR615 User Manual (2026.05, firmware 0.0.0000.36), VISCA and CGI chapters. Autofocus Mode is in this manual only.
Built from the AI Auto Tracking PTZ Camera User Manual for the TR211 / TR315 / TR315N / TR335 / TR335N (2025.12), VISCA and CGI chapters. The Framing tracking mode is set in this manual only.

drivers.name: AVer TR535 / TR535N Dual-Lens Auto Tracking Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: AVer TR535 and TR535N dual-lens AI auto tracking cameras. VISCA over IP (UDP 52381) for power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, exposure, white balance, tally, freeze, auto tracking and tracking mode, theme mode, the HDMI 1 and HDMI 2 sources and the PIP / PBP layout, with every value the camera reports read back; the HTTP CGI for preset save and recall, saturation, contrast, factory reset and the RTMP stream's server, key and status. Both lenses' streams are offered for preview.

help.overview: AVer TR535 / TR535N dual-lens auto tracking cameras for lecture capture and presenter tracking. Power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, exposure, white balance, tally, freeze, auto tracking, theme mode and the HDMI outputs use VISCA over IP; preset save and recall, saturation, contrast, factory reset and the RTMP stream use the camera's web interface (HTTP).
help.setup:
1. Give the camera a fixed IP address.
2. The driver uses two connections to the camera: HTTP on TCP 80 and VISCA over IP on UDP 52381. If you changed the Visca Port Number on the camera (Network page), enter the same number here.
3. If the camera has a web login, enter its username and password. Without them, the commands the camera asks the login for are refused and the device page says so.
4. If the camera answers only HTTPS, turn on HTTPS here and set the HTTP Port to 443.
5. Set Tracking Mode and Set Tracking Body Size use the camera's VISCA special preset numbers. Leave System > VISCA Customized Function at its factory setting for them to work.

compatible_models.notes: Built from the TR535 / TR535N User Manual (2026.05, firmware 0.0.0000.33), VISCA and CGI chapters, and the firmware notes to 0.0.0000.46.

drivers.name: Axis Camera (VAPIX)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Axis network cameras through VAPIX, Axis's own API: remote zoom and focus on fixed cameras, the IR cut filter and day/night switching, image settings, rotation, text and image overlays, the I/O ports, IR illuminators, audio, and the stream and snapshot addresses for the Video Panel. PTZ models add pan, tilt, zoom, presets and guard tours. Port changes, day/night mode, motion, tampering and hardware faults arrive as events.

help.overview: Controls an Axis camera through VAPIX, the camera's own API. Fixed cameras get remote zoom and focus, the IR cut filter and day/night switch, image settings, overlays, the I/O ports and any IR illuminator. PTZ cameras add pan, tilt, zoom, presets and guard tours. Every view area is listed with its stream address so the Video Panel can show it.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera. Axis cameras take a DHCP address and fall back to 192.168.0.90 when no DHCP server answers. The hostname is axis- followed by the serial number, for example axis-b8a44fc359b2.
2. A brand-new camera asks for a root password the first time its web interface opens. Set it before anything else; the camera answers nothing until it is set.
3. Create an account for the driver under System > Accounts with operator or administrator rights, or use root. ONVIF accounts are separate on Axis and do not work here.
4. Check the camera's date and time under System > Date and time. Event timestamps and the camera's own certificate depend on it.
5. Add the camera with its IP address and that login. Under Advanced, pick the view area to control if the camera has more than one, and a stream profile if the Video Panel should use one.
6. To let the Video Panel play the camera's stream without adding it by hand, turn on 'Login in stream address' under Advanced and read the note beside it first.
help.connection: Use a camera account with operator or administrator rights, not an ONVIF account. A new camera needs its root password set in its web interface first. No DHCP? The camera is at 192.168.0.90.

compatible_models.notes: Bench-tested on AXIS OS 10.12: identity, remote zoom and focus, IR cut filter and day/night, image settings, overlays, the I/O ports and their events, view areas with stream and snapshot addresses. It is a fixed dome, so the PTZ, guard tour and IR illuminator control were verified in the simulator only.

models: Any Axis camera on AXIS OS 9.x or later
PTZ models (P55, P56, Q60, Q61, Q62, Q63 series and M55)
compatible_models.notes: Built from the VAPIX documentation. The driver reads what the camera says it has (API discovery, optics capabilities, the port and light rosters) and offers only that. Events need AXIS OS 10.11 or later; older cameras are polled.

tcp_probe.send_ascii:
POST /axis-cgi/basicdeviceinfo.cgi HTTP/1.1
Host: axis
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 66
Connection: close

{"apiVersion":"1.0","method":"getAllUnrestrictedProperties"}

drivers.name: BirdDog PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog PTZ cameras via REST API and VISCA. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets, exposure, white balance, tally, and NDI encode settings.

help.overview:
Controls any BirdDog PTZ camera — P100, P200, P240, P400, A200, A300, X1, MAKI, and newer models. Uses the built-in REST API for configuration and VISCA-over-UDP for real-time PTZ movement.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the camera's IP address (find it via the camera's on-screen display or BirdDog Central).
2. Default REST port is 8080, VISCA port is 52381.
3. No authentication is required.
4. Use 'recall_preset' and 'save_preset' with preset numbers (1-255 depending on model).

drivers.name: Crestron 1 Beyond Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Crestron 1 Beyond IV-CAM cameras (I12, I20, P12, P20 and I12D-B) over VISCA on TCP 5500 or RS-232 / RS-485. Power and Privacy Mode, pan / tilt / zoom / focus, presets, exposure and white balance, tracking and the intelligent modes through the camera's reserved presets, the lightbar, mount mode, and the Intelligent Switching host commands. Publishes each camera's RTSP feeds for the Video Panel.

help.overview: Crestron 1 Beyond IV-CAM cameras over VISCA. Set Model to the camera in hand: the commands offered follow it. Power Off puts the camera in Privacy Mode (video output off, lightbar half red) and Power On wakes it; Crestron's manual says to send Power On before any other command. Start Tracking and Pause Tracking run the intelligent camera's Group Framing or Presenter Tracking, whichever mode Camera Manager set. The camera is polled every few seconds; it does not report changes on its own.
help.setup:
1. Set Model to the camera in hand (the label on the camera or its box).
2. Network: add the camera's IP address. VISCA control uses TCP port 5500.
3. Serial: wire the RS-232 / RS-485 terminal block and use 9600 baud (the camera's OSD can set 2400 to 38400).
4. Set Camera Address to the address in the camera's OSD (System > Address, 1 by default).
5. Set the Home Shot and Tracking Shot (presets 0 and 1) on an intelligent camera before using tracking.
6. Video Panel: set the Camera Password (the one set in Camera Manager) and turn on Login in Stream Address to play the RTSP feeds, or add the stream under Video Streams with its login.

compatible_models.notes: Intelligent cameras. Set Model to I12 or I20. Tracking, Group Tracking (I20), preset zones and tracking profiles (I20) and the Intelligent Switching host commands (I12 in Group Framing) are offered for the model picked.
PTZ cameras. Set Model to P12 or P20 for mount mode and the zoom ratio.
Dual-PTZ speaker-tracking camera. Set Model to I12D-B. Commands reach the PTZ head the camera addresses over VISCA; all three feeds are published.

drivers.name: Epiphan EC20 PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Epiphan EC20 4K PTZ camera over its REST API: power and standby, pan, tilt, zoom and focus with position read-back, presets and home, AI auto-tracking and presenter selection, the tally light, recording, exposure, white balance and picture settings, and RTMP, SRT, multicast and ONVIF streaming. Offers the camera's RTSP stream as a panel preview.

help.overview: Controls an Epiphan EC20 PTZ camera: power and standby, pan, tilt, zoom and focus, presets and the home position, AI auto-tracking and presenter selection, the tally light, recording and freeze. Exposure, white balance, picture, focus, tracking and streaming settings appear on the device page and are read back from the camera, as are the pan, tilt, zoom and focus positions. The camera's RTSP stream is offered to the Video Panel as a preview. The Pan Speed, Tilt Speed, Zoom Speed and Focus Speed fields set the speed of a move that does not give its own.
help.setup:
1. Connect the camera to the network. It takes an address from DHCP and shows it on its front screen; with DHCP off its address is 192.168.100.88.
2. Enter the camera's IP address here with its web user name and password (the factory account is admin, password admin; change it on the camera's web page under System).
3. If the camera's HTTP port was changed under Network > Port, enter it in Port.
4. To show the camera on a panel, leave RTSP authentication off on the camera's Network > RTSP page, and set RTSP Port if it was changed from 554.

compatible_models.notes: EC20 REST API v1 (firmware 3.6.44 was current when this driver was written). Not yet tested on this hardware.

drivers.name: Generic VISCA-IP PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Generic Sony-specification VISCA-over-IP driver (UDP port 52381). Pan/tilt/zoom/focus, presets, auto-exposure, white balance, backlight, power. Covers Sony SRG/BRC, AVer, Marshall, Lumens and many other pro PTZ cameras that adopt Sony's wire format. PTZOptics uses a different framing on TCP/5678 -- prefer the dedicated `ptzoptics` driver for those.

help.overview: Generic Sony-specification VISCA-over-IP PTZ control on UDP port 52381. Supports the universal pan/tilt/zoom/focus + preset + AE/WB command surface. Where a brand-specific driver exists in the catalog, that driver covers more and is preferred.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and place it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. Enable VISCA over IP on the camera (often labeled 'VISCA over IP' or 'IP CONTROL' in the network menu). The default port 52381 should not need to change.
3. Confirm the camera is set to UDP — not TCP. Some cameras let you choose; this driver speaks UDP only.
4. Note: VISCA over IP supports up to 5 simultaneous controllers per camera, so multiple control surfaces (OpenAVC + a hardware joystick + a Bitfocus Companion page, etc.) can co-exist.

compatible_models.notes: Sony's VISCA-over-IP wire format is the de-facto cross-vendor standard for pro PTZ cameras. Brand-specific drivers expose more (vendor-specific image presets, preset-name strings, OSD/menu, lens controls) and should be preferred when available.

Older Sony EVI cameras that speak Sony-spec VISCA-IP but predate the BRC/SRG picture-profile / PRESET MODE / PTZ TRACE / tally surface. For SRG-X400/X402/201M2, SRG-X120/HD1M2, and BRC-X400/X401/H800/H900 use the dedicated `sony_visca` driver instead -- it adds picture profiles, R/B gain, color matrix, defog, PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally, IR correction, AF mode, AE speed, min/max shutter, high sensitivity, and OSD. For the SRG-A40 / SRG-A12 auto framing cameras use `sony_srg_a`.

AVer's published 'VISCA over IP' protocol guide uses UDP 52381 with the Sony 8-byte header (verified against AVer's VISCA Specification 3.3). For the PTZ310 / PTZ330 family use the dedicated `aver_ptz` driver instead -- it adds AVer's HTTP CGI surface (image quality, SmartShoot, SmartFraming, RTMP, bulk status) on top of the VISCA-IP wire format. AVer's TR-series tracking cameras (TR313 and TR315 here) document an HTTP CGI of their own, a different command set from the PTZ310 / PTZ330's, in AVer's TR3XX V2 HTTP CGI Commands and each TR model's user manual. For the TR315 (and the TR615, TR211 and TR335) use the dedicated `aver_tr` driver instead, and for the TR535 / TR535N `aver_tr535`: they add that CGI and read back every value the camera reports. The other TR cameras use this driver for pan, tilt, zoom, presets and power.

Marshall's CV-series broadcast PTZ cameras list VISCA over IP as a control method in their installation manuals. For the CV620-BI/WI, CV620-BI2/WI2, CV625 and CV730 use the dedicated `marshall_ptz` driver instead. It controls them over Marshall's HTTP CGI, with live pan/tilt/zoom/focus read-back, exposure, white balance and focus settings, tally and SRT/RTMP streaming. The CV620-IP and CV620-NDI continue here.

drivers.name: JVC PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls JVC KY-PZ510, KY-PZ400N and KY-PZ200 PTZ cameras over the JVC Web API: pan, tilt and zoom with live position read-back, presets and home, focus, exposure, white balance and picture adjustments, tally, live stream start and stop, the on-screen menu, the KY-PZ510's auto tracking, and the camera's RTSP stream as a panel preview.

help.overview: Controls a JVC KY-PZ PTZ camera over its web API: pan, tilt and zoom, presets and the home position, focus, exposure, white balance and picture adjustments, tally, and starting and stopping the live stream. On a KY-PZ510, auto tracking is turned on and off, its mode picked, and its framing and positions set from here. The live pan, tilt and zoom positions are read back from the camera, and its RTSP stream is offered to the Video Panel as a preview. The camera's power and standby can't be controlled through its web API.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera's IP address on its front LCD (192.168.0.10 from the factory).
2. Open that address in a web browser and sign in as jvc with the factory password 0000; the camera asks for a new password. Set one.
3. Enter the camera's IP address and that password here. Leave the port at 80 unless the camera's HTTP port was changed (Network > Port Settings).
4. To show the camera on a panel, leave RTSP Auth off on the camera's Network page.

compatible_models.notes: Every command in JVC's Web API 1.21 for the KY-PZ510, auto tracking included (firmware 3.0.12 or later). Power and standby are not available through this API. Not yet tested on this hardware.
As the KY-PZ510 without auto tracking. Power and standby are not available through this API. Not yet tested on this hardware.
As the KY-PZ400N without a tally lamp: tally is reported but not controlled. Power and standby are not available through this API. Not yet tested on this hardware.

drivers.name: Marshall PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Marshall IP PTZ cameras over the camera's HTTP CGI: pan, tilt, zoom and focus with live position read-back, presets and home, power and standby, tally, exposure, white balance and picture settings, focus behaviour, pan/tilt limits, SRT and RTMP streaming, and the camera's RTSP stream as a panel preview.

help.overview: Controls a Marshall IP PTZ camera over its web API: pan, tilt, zoom and focus, presets and the home position, power and standby, and tally. Exposure, white balance, picture, focus, motion and streaming settings appear on the device page and are read back from the camera, as are the live pan, tilt, zoom and focus positions. The camera's RTSP stream is offered to the Video Panel as a preview. The Pan/Tilt Speed, Zoom Speed and Focus Speed fields set the speed of a move that does not give its own.
help.setup:
1. Connect the camera to the network and find its address on the camera's on-screen menu (Menu > Ethernet). With DHCP off, Marshall's manual gives 192.168.100.100 as the factory address.
2. Enter the camera's IP address here, with the web user name and password (the camera's factory account is admin, password 9999; change it on the camera's web page under System > User).
3. Leave the port at 80. To use HTTPS instead, turn on Use HTTPS and set the port to 81.
4. To show the camera on a panel, leave RTSP authentication off on the camera's Stream page.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on a CV620-WI2 (firmware VUG115_VUH109): every command and setting read back from the camera. Image mode is reported but fixed at standard on this model; Smart AF is not available.
Marshall publishes the same CGI command document for these cameras. Not yet tested on this hardware.
Earlier CV620 models for which Marshall publishes the same CGI command document. Not yet tested on this hardware.

Named in Marshall's CGI command document, which marks the commands each model lacks (the CV355-30X and CV420-30X take no pan/tilt jog, and the CV420e no focus or iris control). A command the camera does not support is reported as refused. Not yet tested on this hardware.

tcp_probe.send_ascii:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: camera
Connection: close

drivers.name: ONVIF Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls any ONVIF Profile S or Profile T camera or video encoder: pan, tilt, zoom and focus, presets and home, image settings, relay outputs and digital inputs, plus the camera's RTSP stream and snapshot addresses for the Video Panel. Motion, tamper, signal-loss and input changes arrive as events. Use a brand's own driver when the catalog has one; this one covers everything else.

help.overview: ONVIF is the cross-vendor camera control standard. Turn ONVIF on in the camera's web interface, give it an ONVIF user, and add the camera here with that login. The driver reads the camera's make and model, its media profiles (each with a stream address the Video Panel can show), and whatever PTZ, focus, imaging and relay control the camera offers.
help.setup:
1. In the camera's web interface enable ONVIF and create an ONVIF user with administrator or operator rights. Some brands keep ONVIF users separate from web users.
2. Check the camera's date and time. A clock more than a few minutes wrong makes the camera refuse every login; the driver compensates, but only once it can read the clock.
3. Add the camera with its IP address, the ONVIF port (80 on most cameras, 8080 or 8000 on some) and the ONVIF login.
4. Under Advanced, pick a media profile if the camera has more than one and you want PTZ bound to a specific one; the default is the first profile with PTZ.
5. To let the Video Panel play the camera's stream without adding it by hand, turn on 'Login in stream address' under Advanced and read the note beside it first.
help.connection: Enable ONVIF on the camera and use an ONVIF user, not the web login, if the camera keeps them separate. If the login is right and the camera still refuses, set the camera's clock.

compatible_models.notes: Bench-tested on AXIS OS 10.12: identity, three media profiles with stream and snapshot addresses, imaging levels and wide dynamic range, the relay output and the digital input, and the relay and input events. The camera exposes no PTZ over ONVIF and reports no focus move options, so its remote zoom and focus are not reachable through this driver. Create an ONVIF account on the camera first; Axis keeps them separate from web accounts.

models: Any ONVIF Profile S or Profile T conformant camera or encoder
compatible_models.notes: Built from the ONVIF Core, Media, Media2, PTZ, Imaging and Device IO specifications and verified against the simulator. Cameras differ in which services they offer; the driver reads the device's own service list and shows only what it has.

drivers.name: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic AW-HE, AW-UE, and AW-UN series professional PTZ cameras via the documented HTTP CGI protocol (port 80). Covers power, pan/tilt drive and absolute positioning, zoom, focus (auto/manual), iris (auto/ manual), 100 presets, tally, wireless remote enable, and zoom-linked pan/tilt speed, with state changes pushed instantly by the camera's update-notification channel. Image-quality controls (gain, white balance, scene files, gamma) are install-time setup left to the camera's web UI.

help.overview: Panasonic AW-HE/UE/UN are professional PTZ cameras commonly used in broadcast, houses of worship, lecture capture, and corporate AV. The cameras are controlled over HTTP using a small CGI command set. This driver exposes the full pan/tilt/zoom/focus/iris/preset/tally surface needed for live room control. Image quality settings (color, gain, white balance, scene files) are configured in the camera's web UI.
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the camera via its web UI (default credentials
   are typically admin / 12345 — change them).
2. Enter the camera's IP address below. Default port is 80. 3. If you've enabled HTTP authentication on the camera, set Auth Type
   to "basic" and enter the username and password.
4. Pan/tilt drive uses speed values 01..99 per axis (50 = stop, 50/50
   both stop). The home position is APC8000/8000.
5. Presets are numbered 1..100 in the UI; the protocol uses 0..99
   internally, but the driver exposes the 1..100 numbering.
6. Polling is set to 10 seconds by default. Keep this at or above 5 s
   — the cameras throttle aggressive polling and have a 130 ms minimum
   inter-command gap. Changes still show up instantly: the camera
   pushes update notifications the moment anything changes, from any
   controller.
7. Push notifications work by the camera connecting back to the OpenAVC
   server on the Notification Port (31004 by default; several cameras
   can share it). If the server runs a firewall, allow that port
   inbound from the cameras. If the port is blocked, nothing breaks —
   state simply updates at poll speed. Each camera accepts up to 5
   registered receivers; OpenAVC uses one and releases it when the
   device is removed.

compatible_models.notes: Verified end to end on real hardware, including the iris position query (AW-HE145 firmware V01.28, AW-HE40 firmware V1.94).

All AW-HE / AW-UE / AW-UN PTZ models on firmware 4.x+. The AK-UB300 (box camera) is in the same protocol family but does not support most pan/tilt/zoom commands — it returns errors for unsupported operations which the driver simply ignores.

drivers.name: PTZOptics Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls PTZOptics PTZ cameras over the VISCA-over-IP protocol on TCP port 5678. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall / save / reset, tally light, image flip, auto-exposure mode, white balance mode, and backlight. Polled state covers pan / tilt / zoom / focus position, focus mode, AE mode, WB mode, backlight, and flip settings.

help.overview:
PTZOptics cameras are widely used in classrooms, houses of worship, and conference rooms. This driver speaks raw VISCA over TCP 5678 (no Sony VISCA-over-IP header), which is what PTZOptics cameras actually expose — UDP 1259 also works but TCP gives reliable delivery for absolute-position commands.

VISCA is request/response only. The driver polls the camera every few seconds for pan / tilt / zoom / focus position and exposure / WB state. Joystick-style movement uses pt_up / pt_down / etc. with pt_stop to halt; absolute moves use pt_absolute with explicit pan and tilt positions.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera's IP via the OSD menu, the PTZOptics utility, or your router's DHCP table.
2. Confirm VISCA-over-IP is enabled in the camera's web UI (Settings → Network or Settings → VISCA). Most cameras ship with it on by default.
3. Enter the IP in OpenAVC. Port 5678 is fixed.
4. After connecting, pan_position / tilt_position / zoom_position will populate automatically.
5. Save up to 128 presets (numbered 0–127). 'set preset speed' applies to subsequent recalls.

compatible_models.notes: All PTZOptics cameras share the same VISCA-over-IP command set on TCP 5678. Older models may not support every command (the camera ignores unknown ones). 12X-USB needs PTZOptics' IP/serial bridge for network control.

drivers.name: Sony SRG-A40 / SRG-A12 PTZ Auto Framing Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Sony SRG-A40 and SRG-A12 PTZ cameras with PTZ Auto Framing. VISCA over IP (UDP 52381) for power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets 1-64, exposure, white balance, picture, tally and auto framing start and stop, every value the camera reports read back; the web interface (HTTP CGI, Digest login) for presets 1-256 with names, PTZ Auto Framing's settings, compositions and status, RTMP, SRT and NDI|HX streaming, reboot and factory reset. The camera's RTSP, MJPEG and snapshot URLs are offered for preview.

help.overview: Sony SRG-A40 / SRG-A12 PTZ cameras with AI auto framing. Power, pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets 1-64, exposure, white balance, picture, tally and auto framing start and stop use VISCA over IP; presets 65-256 and preset names, the auto framing settings, compositions and status, streaming, reboot and factory reset use the camera's web interface.
help.setup:
1. Give the camera a fixed IP address (RM-IP Setup Tool or the web page's Network menu).
2. Turn on CAMERA SETUP switch 3 (VISCA) on the back of the camera, then power it off and on: without it the camera does not answer VISCA over IP (UDP 52381).
3. Enter the camera's web user name (admin unless you added another) and password. The camera asks for a password the first time anyone signs in to its web page. Settings, power, streaming, Reboot and Factory Reset need an Administrator account; a Full user can run presets and auto framing. Without a login, VISCA control still works.
4. The camera counts wrong passwords and blocks the address after 8 (Brute Force Attack Protection). A refused password is not tried again: correct it here.
5. If the camera answers only HTTPS, turn on HTTPS here and set the HTTP Port to 443.

compatible_models.notes: Built from Sony's VISCA Command List / CGI Command List for the SRG-A40 / A12, Software Version 4.0 (June 2026). The SRG-A12 has optical zoom only (12x). Ball Sports framing, the Lead Room Effect and the composition presets need camera software 4.0.

drivers.name: Sony VISCA-IP PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Dedicated Sony SRG / BRC / EVI VISCA-over-IP driver (UDP port 52381). Adds Sony picture profiles, R/B gain, color matrix, defog, visibility enhancer, low-light, chroma suppress, PRESET MODE + PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, IR correction, ICR, AF mode, AE speed, min/max shutter, high sensitivity, and OSD on/off — on top of the standard PTZ + AE/WB command set.

help.overview: Sony PTZ camera control over VISCA-IP (UDP 52381). Includes Sony's own picture profiles, color matrix, PRESET MODE / PTZ TRACE (BRC-X400/X401), tally, OSD, AF mode, AE speed, IR correction, ICR, and shutter limits.
help.setup:
1. Set the camera to a static IP and put it on a routable VLAN to the OpenAVC server.
2. Enable VISCA over IP in the camera's network menu. The default port 52381 should not need to change.
3. Confirm the camera is set to UDP — not TCP. Sony BRC/SRG cameras default to UDP; this driver speaks UDP only.
4. VISCA over IP supports up to 5 simultaneous controllers per camera, so OpenAVC can co-exist with hardware joysticks or other control surfaces.
5. Picture-profile / color-matrix / defog / PRESET MODE commands only take effect on the BRC-X400/X401 — on smaller SRG models the camera silently rejects them.

compatible_models.notes: BRC-X400 / X401 expose the full feature set (picture profiles, color matrix, defog, PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally). SRG-X400/X402/201M2 and SRG-X120/HD1M2 share the picture profile / R-B gain / chroma suppress / IR correction surface but lack PRESET MODE, PTZ TRACE, tally, color matrix and defog (commands return error harmlessly). BRC-H800 / H900 are older but speak the same Command List wire format. For the SRG-A40 / SRG-A12 auto framing cameras use the sony_srg_a driver: their command list differs and adds PTZ Auto Framing and a web interface (CGI).

drivers.name: Vaddio ConferenceSHOT AV
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Vaddio (Legrand AV) ConferenceSHOT AV conferencing system over its Telnet Serial Command API. Pan/tilt/zoom with absolute positioning and readable position, 16 presets, the full CCU colour and lighting surface, the seven-channel audio mixer as child entities, video mute, indicator LED, IR cut filter, software triggers, IP/USB streaming control with a previewable RTSP stream, and device health.

help.overview: The Vaddio ConferenceSHOT AV is a PTZ camera and audio mixer in one: a 10x optical zoom camera, two EasyMic microphone inputs, a line output for the room speaker, USB 3.0 record and playback, and an H.264 IP stream. This driver drives all of it over the camera's Telnet API — camera moves and presets, colour and lighting, per-channel levels and mutes, video mute for privacy, and the stream itself.
help.setup:
1. TURN TELNET ON FIRST. In the camera's web interface, open Security and enable Telnet access. Vaddio ships it disabled on every firmware issued after mid-December 2019, and nothing on port 23 answers until you enable it.
2. Give the camera a static IP, or reserve its DHCP lease.
3. Enter the IP address, the admin username (default 'admin') and the admin password below. Telnet uses the same admin account as the web interface.
4. Pan, tilt and zoom come in two styles. The drive commands (Pan Left, Tilt Up, Zoom In) keep moving until you send the matching stop, which is what you bind to a press-and-hold button. The position commands (Go To Pan, Go To PTZ Position) move to an absolute angle and are what you bind to a recall.
5. Audio channels appear as sub-devices. Each has a level in dB (-42 to +6) and a mute, so a panel fader binds straight to the channel you mean. Two things about mute are worth knowing before you wire a panel: master mute covers the microphone path only — both EasyMics and the USB record stream — and while it is on the camera refuses to change those three channels one at a time. Standby forces master mute on, so an audio button does nothing until the camera is awake.
6. To see the camera in a Video Panel, turn IP streaming on and the driver publishes the RTSP address for you.

compatible_models.notes: Tested against a ConferenceSHOT AV on firmware 1.7.2. Telnet must be enabled on the web interface's Security page first — it is off by default on every firmware issued after mid-December 2019.

drivers.name: Vaddio RoboSHOT / ConferenceShot
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Vaddio (Legrand AV) RoboSHOT PTZ cameras via the Telnet Serial Command API on port 23. Covers pan/tilt/zoom, focus, 16 presets with Tri-Synchronous Motion, CCU (color / iris / gain / detail / white-balance) controls, factory & custom CCU scenes, and standby. One driver covers the RoboSHOT family — HDBT, HD-SDI, NDI, IW, USB. The ConferenceShot AV has its own driver.

help.overview:
The Vaddio (Legrand AV) RoboSHOT family is one of the most widely deployed PTZ camera lines in commercial AV — boardrooms, lecture capture, courtrooms, broadcast. The Telnet Serial Command API on port 23 lets external controllers drive pan/tilt/zoom, recall the 16 onboard presets (with optional Tri-Synchronous Motion for cinematic moves), tweak iris / gain / white balance, and put the camera in standby. Telnet is disabled on the camera out of the box — turn it on first, on the web interface's Security page.
The ConferenceShot AV is not this driver: its protocol has diverged far enough to need its own, `vaddio_conferenceshot_av`.
help.setup:
1. Turn Telnet on first. In the camera's web interface, open
   Security and enable Telnet access. Vaddio ships it disabled on
   every firmware issued after mid-December 2019, and nothing on
   port 23 answers until you enable it.
2. Set a static IP on the camera in its web interface, or set a
   DHCP reservation in your router.
3. On the same Security page, confirm (or change) the admin
   password. The default is "password" — Vaddio strongly
   recommends changing it.
4. Enter the camera's IP address, the username (default `admin`),
   and the password below. Telnet sessions reuse the same admin
   credentials as the web UI.
5. Pan / tilt / zoom commands are drive-style — they keep moving
   until you send the matching stop. Use the per-axis "stop"
   commands or the per-axis variable-speed drive commands with
   speed=0 to halt.
6. The 16 pan/tilt/zoom presets (camera preset recall N) are
   saved in the camera. Use Tri-Synchronous Motion (the optional
   `tri-sync` speed parameter on store) for smooth simultaneous
   pan/tilt/zoom moves between presets.
7. CCU (color / lighting) values follow Vaddio's documented ranges:
   iris 0-11, gain 0-11, detail 0-15, chroma 0-14, red_gain and
   blue_gain 0-255. red/blue gain are only writable when auto white
   balance is off; iris and gain are only writable when auto-iris
   is off; backlight compensation conflicts with wide dynamic range.

compatible_models.notes:
The RoboSHOT family shares one Telnet API. Vaddio is now part of Legrand AV — older boxes still ship as "Vaddio". Speed ranges (pan 1-24, tilt 1-20, zoom 1-7, focus 1-8) and CCU value ranges are consistent across the RoboSHOT line.
The ConferenceShot AV is NOT covered here and has its own driver, `vaddio_conferenceshot_av`. Checking it against hardware showed the two protocols have diverged: the ConferenceShot AV has a seven-channel audio mixer, readable absolute pan/tilt/zoom, video mute, LED and IR-cut control and a CCU gamma value that this driver does not carry, and it does NOT have the CCU scenes or Tri-Synchronous Motion presets that this driver sends. Take the ConferenceShot 10 and FX as unverified for the same reason: the ConferenceShot line should not be assumed to match RoboSHOT until each is read against its own manual or a unit.
